question: For a person with Hypermetropia or far-sightedness, the near point, is ______ farther away from the normal near point.
solution:
The correct answer is__** 25 cm.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hypermetropia,** also known as **far-sightedness**, is a common vision condition where distant objects can be seen more clearly than near objects.
 
• In hypermetropia, the near point of vision is farther away than the normal near point, which is typically around **25 cm** for a person with normal vision.
 
• This condition occurs when the eye is too short, or the cornea has too little curvature, preventing light rays from focusing correctly on the retina.
 
• People with hypermetropia may experience difficulty in reading or performing close-up tasks without corrective lenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Symptoms**: Common symptoms of hypermetropia include eye strain, headaches, and difficulty focusing on nearby objects.
 
• **Correction**: Hypermetropia can be corrected with prescription eyeglasses or contact lenses that are convex, which help focus light onto the retina.
 
• **Prevalence**: This condition can occur in people of all ages but is more common in younger children and can decrease with age as the eye's lens becomes less flexible.
 
• **Diagnosis**: An eye examination by an optometrist or ophthalmologist is necessary to diagnose hypermetropia and determine the appropriate corrective measures.
